text: Most health insurance claims in India get rejected, so why pay for a policy
Most health insurance claims in India get rejected, so why pay for a policy
Most health insurance claims in India get rejected, so I shouldn't pay for a policy.

chain.why: According to IRDAI Annual Report 2024–25, para I.6.5.6 and Table I.29, 87% of health claims were paid and only 8% were rejected, showing that most claims are approved.
According to IRDAI data for 2023–24, as reported by IndiaMedToday, 83% of health claims were settled and 11% repudiated, confirming that the majority of claims are paid.

According to National Health Accounts Estimates 2022–23, NHSRC/MoHFW, May 2026, households paid about 43% of total health spending out of pocket, indicating a large financial exposure without insurance.
According to MoSPI/NSO, NSS 80th round press note, 20 Apr 2026, 44.3% of urban residents had any health insurance, so more than half had none.

conclusion: Since the majority of claims are paid and many people lack any coverage, the belief that most claims are rejected is inaccurate and a personal policy can address the uncovered risk.
